applies_why: Yes, because the judge treats the collision as unresolved by the absence of an explicit textual statement of paternity, which is what K-C governs.
quote: where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: 'that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires.' Reading 1: the judge may not use absence of an explicit verse resolving/contradicting a point; chain-vs-chain footing controls. Reading 2: only the demand for a single contrary verse is retired, so an underdetermined chain-vs-chain result can still rest on lack of explicit textual resolution.
why: The judge declares the link underdetermined because there is no explicit textual resolution of paternity, which is the retired stating-verse test rather than a chain-against-chain footing.
